Brachial plexus: C5-T1 roots merge & divide → median · ulnar & radial n.
Traumatic (MC: MVC · falls - stretch from force pulling shoulder up or pushing down): burner (stinger) · backpack palsy · root avulsions
Nontraumatic: cervical ribs · tumors · inflam (neuralgic amyotrophy/Parsonage-Turner) · neurogenic thoracic outlet · radiation · DM
Downward force on shoulder → superior roots → shoulder & elbow funct loss
▪︎T1 MC w hyperextension (most inferior - most pulled): finger abduction/adduction · thumb opposition · wrist flex · sensation ulnar forearm
ddx C7 root: finger flex/ext · wrist flex · elbow ext - sensation thumb · index & middle fingers
ddx median n.: thumb opposition (⍉finger abduction) - sensation palmar thumb · index & middle fingers
▪︎EMG later to define neuropathy - denervation detectable ~3wks after inj
Stretch/contusion: PT (strengthening · prevent contractures) - improvement USU w.in 3mo
▪︎⍉improvement → surg (n. reconstruction or transfer) - improves only ~60%
Common peroneal n. courses around fibular head → superficial & deep peroneal n.
Eti: inj or compress @ prox fibula - fibular head frx · knee inj/dislocation · casting P · operative positioning · leg crossing
Deep peroneal: sensation b/n 1st & 2nd toes - tibialis anterior (dorsiflexion & inversion) · extensor hallucis longus (great toe ext)
Superficial peroneal: peroneus longus (eversion) - sensation most of dorsal foot
ddx tibial n. inj (popliteal fossa): ↓calf sensation · weak plantar flex
ddx ↓dorsalis pedis pulse: tibia or knee inj (popliteal a. → anterior tibial a. → dorsalis pedis) - posterior tibial a. ← popliteal a. via tibioperoneal trunk
DX: thorough neurovasc exam distal to any suspected frx (strength · sensation · blood flow)
Frx w neurovasc compromise → emergent reduction & ortho Refer
